question: What is the recognized age range for adolescence according to the World Health Organization?
explanation: Adolescence is globally defined by the World Health Organization as the period between 10 and 19 years of age. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why are teenagers often more at risk for reproductive health issues?

options.A: Biological maturity happens faster than financial and social independence
options.B: They always have free and easy access to healthcare
options.C: They are naturally immune to sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Physical growth slows down completely during the teen years

explanation: Young people reach sexual maturity while still dependent on adults economically and socially, which creates barriers to accessing proper care. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which part of the brain matures later in teenagers, affecting their impulse control?
explanation: The prefrontal cortex develops slower than emotional brain centers, which contributes to risk-taking behavior in teenagers. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h2)

question: A teenager takes sexual risks despite knowing better. What best explains this behavior?

options.A: Nerves in the skin stop working properly
options.B: The brain's emotional center develops faster than the planning center
options.C: They have fully thought through all long-term outcomes
options.D: Puberty completely stops sex hormone production

explanation: Emotions and reward-seeking drive actions faster than the logical planning part of the brain can restrain them during these years. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is cervical ectopy in adolescent females?

options.A: Complete closing of the opening to the womb
options.B: Immature cervical cells exposed on the outer surface
options.D: A harmless tumor found during routine pelvic exams

explanation: Cervical ectopy means delicate glandular cells are exposed on the outer cervix, making young females more vulnerable to certain infections. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h3)

question: What factor most commonly stops adolescents from seeking treatment for infections?

options.A: Parents must legally approve every single lab test
options.B: Fear of judgment and stigma from healthcare workers
options.C: Medication is guaranteed free at every local pharmacy
options.D: Diseases never show any physical signs at all

explanation: Stigma and judgmental attitudes from clinic staff often prevent youths from asking for medical help when they need it. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why is obstructed labor more common in very young adolescent mothers?

options.A: The thyroid gland works too fast
options.B: The pelvis is not yet fully grown
options.C: Bones in the skull close too early
options.D: The mother is usually very tall and heavy

explanation: An immature pelvis is often too small for a safe vaginal delivery, which can lead to obstructed labor. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why are pregnant teenagers at high risk for severe anemia?

options.A: Fetal development actively destroys the mother's blood cells
options.B: The body stops making red blood cells during pregnancy
options.C: Iron supplements are illegal for anyone under twenty
options.D: The growing baby and the young mother compete for nutrients

explanation: Because the teenager's own body is still growing, her nutritional needs clash with the high demands of the developing fetus. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is a dangerous physical result of unsafe, hidden abortions among teenagers?

options.A: The body becomes immune to future pregnancies
options.C: Pelvic floor muscles become much stronger

explanation: Unsafe procedures done by unqualified persons frequently cause severe internal bleeding and damage to reproductive organs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h5)

question: How do social pressures worsen the problem of unsafe abortions in young girls?

options.A: Traditional rules force immediate hospital stays for minors
options.B: Stigma forces them to hide pregnancies and seek dangerous care
options.C: Communities give out money for safe medical care
options.D: Culture requires male partners to take full legal blame

explanation: Fear of punishment and social rejection drives adolescents to hide their condition and use risky methods to end pregnancies. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h5)

question: In the HEADSS adolescent health assessment tool, what do the two 'S' letters stand for?
explanation: The HEADSS framework covers Sexuality and Suicide or depression as vital screening areas for teenagers. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h6)

question: A 16-year-old girl comes to the clinic with her mother. What is the best nursing action during the visit?

options.A: Refuse to examine the patient unless her father is present
options.B: Wait until the patient turns 18 to do any evaluation
options.C: Share everything the teen says with the mother right away
options.D: Interview the teenager privately for part of the visit

explanation: Private interview time helps build trust and encourages honest talk about sensitive health topics. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is a key feature of youth-friendly reproductive health services?

options.A: Strict appointment times that conflict with school hours
options.B: High fees to pay for clinic upkeep
options.C: Staff trained in confidentiality and teenage psychology
options.D: Parents must be present for every single consultation

explanation: Youth-friendly centers rely on confidential care and staff who understand adolescent behavior and needs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why is peer-led health education effective for teaching teenagers about reproductive health?

options.A: Teens relate better to messages from people their own age
options.B: Young people hold official degrees in medicine
options.C: It removes all biological risks of sexual activity
options.D: Peer educators completely replace regular hospitals

explanation: Adolescents often trust health information more when it comes from peers who share similar experiences. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h7)
